title: A Randomized Trial to Determine the Effect of Flavored, Sweetened Water With Electrolytes on Fluid Balance in Women
official: A Randomized Trial to Determine the Effect of Flavored, Sweetened Water With Electrolytes on Fluid Balance in Women
summary: Electrolytes, such as sodium and potassium, are minerals found in many beverages. Drinks that contain electrolytes may help the body retain more of the fluid that is consumed. Most previous research on these types of beverages has been conducted in athletes during or after exercise, when people are already dehydrated. Less is known about how these beverages affect hydration during typical daily activities that involve mostly sitting with occasional light walking. This study will compare two flavored waters containing electrolytes with plain water to determine their effects on hydration in healthy women.

interventions.name: Flavored, sweetened water with electrolytes containing less sodium
Flavored, sweetened water with electrolytes containing more sodium

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria

* Subject is female
* Subject is not pregnant (confirmed via urine pregnancy test) or breastfeeding
* Subject is 18-65 years of age, inclusive
* Subject engages in routine physical activity (goes for a walk at least 2 times per week and goes to the gym or participates in a workout/dance class or sport at least 1 time per week)
* Subject does not smoke (or has quit for at least 6 months)
* Subject is not taking medication that may interfere with the study (e.g., diuretics, laxatives, weight loss drugs)
* Subject has no health conditions that would interfere with the study (e.g. cardiovascular, renal, or metabolic diseases)
* Subject is not allergic or averse to consuming pineapple orange mango flavoring
* Subject is not allergic to Stevia
* Subject is willing to avoid alcohol consumption 24 hours prior to visits
* Subject is willing to fast and restrict fluids, including water for 12 hours (overnight) prior to visits
* Subject is willing to refrain from vigorous exercise for 24 hours
* Subject is willing to eat the exact same food the day prior to each study session.
* Subject is able to speak, write, and read English, provide consent to participate in the study, and comply with all study procedures and scheduled visits

Exclusion Criteria

* Subject has participated in a clinical trial within the past 30 days
* Subject has participated in any PepsiCo trial within past 3 months
* Subject has a condition or is taking medication that the investigator believes would interfere with his/her ability to provide informed consent, comply with the study protocol, which might confound the interpretation of the study results, or put the person at undue risk
* Subject is employed by PepsiCo. Subject is employed by, or has a parent, guardian, or other immediate family member employed by a company that manufactures any products that compete with any Gatorade product. If subject is unsure if a company would be considered a competitor to Gatorade, they will be asked to please let the study investigator know the name of the other company and the nature of their relationship to that company before they sign the informed consent.
